title: Finite-cell left dg modules and the integer coefficient sheaf on a point
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B$ be a category essentially small in the coefficient universe $u$, $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $B$, $S$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $A$ a left sheaf dg $S$-algebra, and $P$ a left dg $A$-module, using [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Say that $P$ has a finite-cell filtration if there are an integer $t\geq0$, dg modules $F_{-1},F_0,\ldots,F_t$, and injective dg maps $f_j:F_{j-1}\to F_j$ for $0\leq j\leq t$, with $F_{-1}=0$, an isomorphism $F_t\cong P$, and dg isomorphisms $\operatorname{coker}(f_j)\cong\bigoplus_{a\in\{0,\ldots,n_j-1\}}A[k_{ja}]$ for natural numbers $n_j$ and integers $k_{ja}$. The inclusions into $P$ are the composites followed by the final isomorphism; thus these data are a filtration by dg submodules of $P$. The regular left module and integer shifts are those of the cited localization node, including the signed shifted left action. Empty sums, repeated stages and $P=0$ are allowed. For ordinary dg algebras over $\mathbf Z$, use the terminal category $B$ with its trivial topology and the constant sheaf with sole value $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z)$; denote this coefficient sheaf by pointIntegers. This site presents sheaves on a point.
